subject: trying to "colsplit" on a factor containing "."

messages.author: 18636d58f7894a34
messages.subject: trying to "colsplit" on a factor containing "."
parts:
This seems like it should be trivial but I haven't figured out a solution:

Works:
x <- c("a_1", "a_2", "b_2", "c_3")
varsx <- colsplit(x, "_", c("trt", "time"))
varsx
  trt time
1   a    1
2   a    2
3   b    2
4   c    3

Fails:
y <- c("a.1", "a.2", "b.2", "c.3")
varsy <- colsplit(x, ".", c("trt", "time"))
varsy
  trt time NA.
1  NA   NA  NA
2  NA   NA  NA
3  NA   NA  NA
4  NA   NA  NA


Any ideas? 

Perhaps more importantly, can anyone point me at a good resource for doing basic string manipulations like this?  I seem run into issues of improper variable names, say containing "-" quite often and a primer on what the basic ground rules are for R would be helpful.

Thanks!

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: trying to "colsplit" on a factor containing "."
parts:
Try colsplit(x, fixed("."), c("trt", "time")). You might want to have
a look at the stringr article in the R journal:
http://journal.r-project.org/archive/2010-2/RJournal_2010-2_Wickham.pdf

Hadley

messages.author: 373beb702917b8b5
messages.subject: Re: trying to "colsplit" on a factor containing "."
parts:
Hi,

I think the basic thing you're missing is that pattern (the second
argument to colsplit) is a regular expression. In regexp the . matches
any character, which is probably not what you want. To match a literal
. use \\. like this:

varsy <- colsplit(y, "\\.", c("trt", "time"))

Best,
Ista
